# Culmina components

Use for composing, correcting or documenting existing Flutter controls and displays. Read [AGENTS](../../../AGENTS.md) and inspect the affected source/caller before choosing a component.

| Task | Reference | Preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field, action, choice, confirmation or deletion | [Forms](references/forms.md) | Units, validation, edited drafts and Save/Discard/Cancel |
| Context actions, detail template or destination | [Navigation](references/navigation.md) | Actual route adoption, Back/state and no-site semantics |
| Fit/state, disclosure, measurement or science graphic | [Data display](references/data-display.md) | Unknown, fit versus persistence/result state and source-owned calculations |

Read only the relevant group. Reuse the current component before adding an abstraction; inspect loading, missing-input, disabled, error and saved/changed states. Component availability or a gallery example does not prove production adoption.

For a changed contract, describe its purpose, inputs, states, interactions, semantics and real adopter. Preserve full labels, reachable actions, natural text growth and existing theme roles. A local component fix does not imply a routing redesign.

Report the source/caller, changed behavior, actual checks and limits. Native host renders, Android/device interaction and owner acceptance are separate evidence.

Use when a UI task affects product meaning, scientific inputs, missing data or persistence. Start from [AGENTS](../../../AGENTS.md), the affected screen/ViewModel and domain service; current code supplies behavior, while the user supplies task scope.

- Unknown is not zero. Retain units, source/freshness and theoretical versus empirical storage meaning. Relative stacking gain is not absolute SNR; AF/MF describes focusing and supplies no numeric focus measurement.
- Preserve Capture Plan assumptions, calibration policies, exposure/filter groups and fit reasons. Follow actual camera-class validation rather than hiding inconvenient inputs.
- Fit, working draft, explicitly saved plan and recorded result are distinct. Trace state through `lib/presentation/viewmodels/` and actual confirmation/caller behavior; keep Save/Discard/Cancel and failure recovery.
- Core planning, catalog and local records must remain usable offline. Preserve cache timestamps and missing/stale weather distinctions. Label illustrative fixtures as examples.
- Support Light, Dark and Field Red using `lib/core/theme/` and the field filter in `lib/main.dart`. Inspect pairing/readability in the intended theme; source colors alone do not establish accessibility acceptance.

Use `.audit/atlas/` only as historical visual evidence and identify its captured state. It supplies neither current implementation requirements nor approval for a new direction. The reserved `design/` directory currently contains no browser prototype.

Report the affected invariant, owning source/caller, change or review finding, checks and remaining limits. Keep unrelated findings separate from the requested implementation.

Paths are relative to the repository root. Unqualified shared filenames are under `lib/presentation/shared/`; `widgets/` means `lib/presentation/widgets/`. Values come from existing domain/ViewModel contracts.

| API/source | Inputs, variants and slots | State and interaction contract | Adopter/check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DocumentSection` in `document_section.dart` | Required existing `children`; optional padding (16 dp), joinPrevious/joinNext for lazy month slices | Flat surfaceSubtle, radius 8 dp, zero elevation. No new callback, clipping, semantic merging or fixed text height. Local Material preserves child ink/focus feedback. Keep source-owned chart/calendar widths and all existing actions | Tonight, Plan, Logbook, Night, Moon, Weather, Library, Settings, Record result; `test/presentation/shared/document_section_test.dart` |
| `SkyDarknessWidget` in `widgets/sky_darkness_widget.dart` | `embedded:false` keeps standalone framing; `embedded:true` uses the containing document group's frame/inset | Same remembered disclosure key, top sibling rule, Bortle/SQM/Unknown, independent provenance, picker and external-map action in both variants | Planner `home_screen.dart` uses embedded; `sky_darkness_context_test.dart` covers standalone facts and embedded control/persistence behavior |
| `StatusBlock` in `lib/presentation/shared/status_block.dart` | Required `state:FitState`; optional `needed/usable:Duration?`, `reason`, `missing`, `keyNumbers:List<(String,String)>`, `action:Widget?` | Only show measured headline when both durations exist. Missing input uses its word, never fabricated zero. Action slot is caller-owned; the widget calculates nothing | `test/presentation/shared/status_block_test.dart`; Tonight instance; planner `plan_status.dart` uses `StatusBlock.headline` only; isolated trial |
| `PlanStateLabel(PlanState)` in `plan_state.dart` | States: notSaved, saved, savedChanged, tracking, completed, partly, notDone, oldLog. `PlanState.from` consumes status/savedBefore/legacy and optional resultKind | Persistence/result state is distinct from fit; do not infer “Saved” from “Fits”. Result states have existing icons. Current code supports partly; historical adoption text predates that implementation | Native gallery and `test/presentation/shared/plan_state_test.dart`; Logbook/planner |
| `CollapsibleSection` in `collapsible_section.dart` | Required sectionKey/title/child; optional summary/initiallyOpen; remembered form or controlled pair `open` **and** `onToggle` | Supply both controlled properties together; otherwise retain DisclosureViewModel. Closed child is not built. Summary remains visible; header has expanded semantics and 48 dp target. Reduced motion omits AnimatedSize | `test/presentation/shared/collapsible_section_test.dart`; isolated trial |
| `ChangeMark` in `change_mark.dart` | Required value and child; value change triggers the existing transient cue | Does not persist or compute domain state. Preserve the original value/change boundary and reduced-motion behavior | `test/presentation/widgets/capture_outputs_test.dart` and actual planner callers |
| `AltitudeChartWidget` in `widgets/altitude_chart_widget.dart` | Required opportunity; optional moonAltitudesDeg, zoneId, nowUtc, captureEndUtc; `TimelineDensity.full/compact` | Full has grid/legend; compact retains timing information. Existing painter/timeline data owns scientific geometry. Use chart tokens, not approximate CSS astronomy | `test/presentation/design_system/u_renders_test.dart`; `widgets/tonight_opportunity_widget.dart` contains a call, but that wrapper has no production instantiation at this snapshot; current night-browser timeline is separate |
| `StackingGainGraph` in `widgets/capture_plan/stacking_gain_graph.dart` | Required curve and groupLabel; optional caption and recorded frame count | Graph is relative improvement over integration time normalized to the plan (1.00×), with plan/comparison and optional recorded marks. Preserve the existing curve and per-group exposure/filter meaning; no absolute SNR or universal score. Hybrid functional gradients are presentation, not new science | `widgets/capture_plan/capture_budget_summary.dart`; existing graph/curve checks and planner |
| `NightBarSection` in `widgets/night_browser_sections.dart` | Existing browser ViewModel/site providers; `compact`, `home` presentation flags | Two exact-boundary jump actions, 16 dp before the 48 dp slider region. Current instant/state stays visible. Legend, encoding warning and exact intervals are behind the initially closed `Exact times & reading key` action; opening it changes no preview/plan data. Preserve sky/Moon lanes and five-minute browse semantics | Tonight and Night & Moon detail; `night_moon_browse_test.dart`, actual screen callers and corresponding render fixtures |

`WeatherDetailsTable(rows:, background:)` in `widgets/weather_details_table.dart` implements the current Forecast details composition. It accepts the caller's nine existing cell widgets/row decorations and document surface color. One intrinsic `Table` fixes its leading Local time column at 96 dp; its actual render children keep painting, hit tests and semantic bounds synchronized during horizontal scroll. Row heights follow full text and the user's scaler without a second layout/measurement loop. Per-cell semantics retain reading order and expose metric cells beside time when accessibility requests reveal. Only the Weather details caller adopts it; loading/unavailable/no-dark branches, model/provenance, units, dated offsets/DST, unknowns and partial-hour qualifications remain caller-owned. `weather_fixed_time_test.dart` covers three themes/phone widths, scaling/direction/update smoke, reveal, exact metric/imperial DST readouts and snapshot integrity. The widget test does not establish physical-device, owner or TalkBack acceptance.

Use `NightTimeFormatter` / `QuantityText` and the existing word helpers for dates, units and labels. For every touched component record the needed variant, state, slots, input provenance and relevant check; do not analyse every category for an unrelated change.

Paths below are relative to the repository root. Unqualified shared filenames are under `lib/presentation/shared/`; `app_button_styles.dart` is under `lib/core/theme/`. Inspect the named API before editing; this index routes to source and does not replace it.

| `site_form_input.dart`, `target_form_input.dart`, `rig_input_text.dart` | Existing domain validators and field copy; inspect the relevant methods rather than inventing another API | Keep units, range errors, camera-class requirements and edited drafts. Field loading/error/disabled presentation belongs to the adopting form | Existing site/target/rig editor tests; search by class name |
| `askUnsavedChanges(context, plan: ...)` in `confirmation_patterns.dart` | Returns `UnsavedChoice.save/discard/cancel`; `plan` required | Cancel/back/outside = cancel. Caller performs Save/Discard and handles failure; prompt itself does not persist | `test/presentation/design_system/design_system_gallery_test.dart`; planner leaving flow |
| `confirmDestructive(context, title:, message:, action:)` in same source | Required item-specific title and consequence; action defaults to Delete | True only for explicit confirmation; false on cancellation/dismissal. No destructive work inside the prompt | Native gallery overlay checks |
| `DeleteButton`, `SwipeToDelete`, `showUndo` in `delete_patterns.dart` | Button: tooltip/onPressed; swipe: itemKey/onDelete/child; undo: message/onUndo | Swipe/button delegate to the adopter. Stored-record confirmation differs from an editable-plan Undo. Respect existing stale-recovery guards in the actual caller | Native gallery and existing delete/Undo task tests |

For selection: radio/segments express one of a few mutually exclusive values; searchable select expresses a larger single-choice set; checkboxes express independent selections; switches apply a binary setting. An option count does not change the underlying choice semantics. Error text must name the problem and recovery; colour is additional information.

For a requested component comparison, inspect the existing control/caller and compare concrete input/state behavior using identical content. Historical examples do not replace current source.

rules.text: **Tonight:** `lib/presentation/screens/tonight/tonight_home_screen.dart` (`_Context`) passes `compact:true`, `noSiteLabel:ContextLine.setSite` ("Set site"), the compact `SiteLabel` display and full `siteDescription:SiteLabel.of(siteVm)`. It leaves `framed:false` at its default, passes `planVm.eveningDate` and `zoneId`, and omits `nightStartUtc`, so no inline zone caption appears. `onSite/onNight` call `showHomeSiteSheet/showHomeNightSheet` in `home_context_sheets.dart`: Manage sites and the direct calendar respectively (TD-120).

**No site:** callers must supply `night:null` and no night instant; the component does not infer those from a null name. The site action remains available as "Set site"; default component wording remains "No site set". Never compute a night for the placeholder location.

**Accessibility and layout:** each choice retains a 48 × 48 logical px minimum, an enabled button semantics action, its own Choose a site/night hint and a full-label tooltip. Compact choices follow their content with a 4 dp gap; the site flexes/ellipsizes when needed and the date keeps its natural width. Compact site semantics use `siteDescription ?? siteName ?? ContextLine.noSite`, while the default wrapping variant uses `siteName ?? ContextLine.noSite`. `noSiteLabel` changes visible wording, not the semantic fallback. Both variants expose the full "Night of …" label; `siteDescription` affects only compact site semantics/tooltip. `framed:true` remains an optional `context.card` wrapper for either variant, not a requirement for a screen.

# Native semantic role map

Current mapping guidance carried forward from the 2026-10-24 token/source reconciliation, not a new token authority. Read only the roles needed by the task and inspect their definition and actual caller. Repository paths below are relative to the root. [AGENTS](../../../../AGENTS.md) describes the shared source routes and evidence limits.

| Semantic role | Production source | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surface-default` | `Theme.of(context).scaffoldBackgroundColor` (`ThemeData`) | The page canvas |
| `surface-subtle` | `HybridTokens.surfaceSubtle`; generic theme surfaces remain `ColorScheme.surface` and field `cardColor` | Quiet Hybrid grouping; selected root navigation and Concept B `DocumentSection` use this role. Field `ColorScheme.surface` is black, while `surfaceSubtle` and `cardColor` use the dark-red grouping surface |
| `surface-raised` | `AppPalette.surfaceRaised`, `surfaceContainerHigh` | Dialogs, menus and sheets above the page |
| `surface-sunken` | `HybridTokens.surfaceSunken` | Recessed Moon-lane tracks and the Moon-up legend well in `night_browser_sections.dart`; distinct from raised overlays |
| `text-primary` | `AppPalette.textPrimary` | Answers, values and meaningful headings |
| `text-secondary` | `AppPalette.textSecondary` | Labels and supporting explanations |
| `text-tertiary` | `AppPalette.textTertiary` | Provenance, time zone and freshness; never hide necessary instructions here |
| `text-disabled` | `AppPalette.textDisabled` | Disabled controls only, not normal metadata |
| `border-subtle` | `AppPalette.border` | Decorative dividers and group outlines |
| `border-control` | `AppPalette.controlBorder`, `ColorScheme.outline` | A boundary needed to recognise a control |
| `status-*` | `AppPalette.statusFits/Tight/DoesNotFit/NoWindow/Neutral` via `FitText.color` | Fit verdicts in `StatusBlock`; retain the status word and reason |
| `state-*` | `AppPalette.stateUnsaved/Settled/Quiet` for `PlanState.tone`; compact badges use the Hybrid pairs below | Persistence/result state, distinct from fit; a tone helper is not the badge's current colour map |

Not recorded (`EntryStateBadge.due`) uses caution. These are state words, not fit or image-quality verdicts |
| Selected weather hour | `HybridTokens.selectedHourFill/selectedHourText/selectedHourRule` | `weather_hybrid_view.dart` hour axis: fill, text and bottom rule, with selected semantics. `hourBackground/hourText` exist but have no presentation callers at this baseline; do not substitute them |

# Culmina — shared agent instructions

Culmina is a Flutter/Dart Android astrophotography planner and observing log.
The technical Dart package is `astroplan`; keep existing imports and identifiers.
Plan a night, site, target and rig; save a Capture Plan; record imaging results.
The app does not control cameras or mounts.

## Source and scope

- This file is the shared instruction source for Codex, Claude and Gemini.
- Follow the current user task; skills and archived findings are not a task queue.

## Architecture map

- `lib/main.dart`: startup, catalog seeding and concrete dependency composition.

flutter run
flutter analyze --no-pub
flutter test --no-pub

# Design system

This is a reference to the implemented Flutter UI in `lib/`.
It does not assert visual or accessibility acceptance.

## Design guidance structure

Use the relevant one of the five local Culmina design skills. They have distinct
scopes; supporting references and implementation files are not additional rule sets.
Shared product invariants remain in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

| Local skill | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| [Components](../.agents/skills/culmina-design-components/SKILL.md) | Existing components, states, callbacks and actual adopters |
| [Product rules](../.agents/skills/culmina-design-rules/SKILL.md) | Scientific meaning, time, missing data and persistence distinctions |
| [Spacing](../.agents/skills/culmina-design-spacing/SKILL.md) | Local geometry, shape, density and reduced motion |
| [Tokens](../.agents/skills/culmina-design-tokens/SKILL.md) | Semantic colors and surfaces across all three themes |
| [Typography](../.agents/skills/culmina-design-typography/SKILL.md) | Adopted text roles, wrapping, scaling and numeric readability |

This document indexes the implementation. The skills' supporting references route
to current definitions and callers. Compatibility files in `.agents/rules/` point
back to shared guidance; external design playbooks and archived recipes are not
automatically adopted Culmina policy. A component specimen demonstrates appearance
in its captured state, not production adoption or device acceptance.

## Theme sources

- `core/theme/app_theme.dart`: Light, Dark and red Field `ThemeData`.
- `app_colors.dart`: raw colors; `app_palette.dart`: semantic theme extension.
- `hybrid_tokens.dart`: additional surfaces, selection, feedback, chart colors,
  compact type sizes, minimum target and app-bar height.
- `app_typography.dart`, `app_spacing.dart`, `app_radius.dart`,
  `app_motion.dart`: type, spacing, shape and transition values.
- `app_button_styles.dart`: shared button styling.

`DisplaySettingsViewModel` stores System/Light/Dark appearance and display
choices. `ThemeViewModel` stores field mode separately. `main.dart` selects
the theme and applies `AppTheme.fieldFilter` around app content in field mode.

## Base colors

| Role | Light | Dark | Field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `#FFFFFF` | `#191919` | `#000000` |
| Surface | `#F7F7F5` | `#202020` | `#110000` |
| Raised surface | `#FFFFFF` | `#252525` | `#1A0000` |
| Primary text | `#37352F` | `#EBEBEA` | `#FF0000` |
| Secondary text | `#5A5955` | `#A5A5A3` | `#AA0000` |
| Border | `#E9E9E7` | `#2F2F2F` | `#330000` |

`AppPalette` adds semantic event/chart roles. `HybridTokens` supplies action,
accent, success/caution/error and selected-hour roles. These are separate
from base surfaces; component callers resolve the relevant token set.

## Typography

Production text roles use the bundled **Geist** family.
Source Serif 4 is bundled in `pubspec.yaml` but is not the production role family.

| `AppTypography` role | Size / line height | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `screenTitle` | 22 / 27.5 | 500 |
| `sectionHeading` | 20 / 28 | 600 |
| `sectionSubject` | 18 / 23.4 | 500 |
| `itemTitle` | 16 / 22.4 | 600 |
| `rowTitle` | 16 / 24 | 500 |
| `value` | 15 / 21.75 | 400 |
| `body` | 14 / 21.7 | 400 |
| `caption` | 13 / 19.5 | 400 |
| `dense` | 12 / 18 | 400 |
| `navigationLabel` | 11 / 16.5 | Caller selects 400/600 |

Additional heading roles are `homeHeading` (29), `nightHeading` (25)
and `answerHeading` (28). `AppTypography.scale` also defines the Material
`TextTheme`; it is distinct from the named screen roles.
Compact calendar/chart token sizes are 10/11 logical pixels.

## Layout, shape and motion

- `AppSpacing`: 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48; page gutter 20 and section gap 28.
  Additional compact steps are 2, 3, 6, 10, 12 and 14.
- `AppRadius`: small 6, menu 8, large 12 and pill 999.
- `HybridTokens`: minimum target 48; app bar height 64.
- `AppMotion`: short 120 ms, medium 180 ms, highlight 1500 ms;
  curve `Cubic(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
  Its duration helper returns zero when platform animations are disabled.
- `AppShell`: four navigation items with minimum height 56;
  at text scale 1.5 or greater it lays them out two per row.

## Shared UI

`presentation/shared/` contains the app bar, line icons, section headers,
collapsible sections, detail scaffold, status/failure feedback, confirmation
and deletion patterns, field-mode control and form-input helpers.
`presentation/widgets/` contains altitude/night/weather visualizations,
capture planning, budgets, fit/status and storage/gain presentation.
Screen-specific layouts live under `presentation/screens/`.

The current composition is Tonight → separate Plan/detail flows, with
Logbook, Library and Settings as other root destinations.
Labels, unknown-data messages and draft/result distinctions come from
shared text helpers and the relevant screen/ViewModel state.

See [Product specification](PRODUCT_SPEC.md) and [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md).

# Product specification

Culmina plans astrophotography sessions and records their outcomes.
This document describes implemented behavior in `lib/`, not a release plan.

## Main flow

Choose site and evening date → choose target and rig → inspect the night →
edit capture blocks → review budget/fit → save → image outside the app →
record a result and review it in Logbook.

## Screens

| Screen | Current behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Welcome | First-run setup and entry into planning. |
| Tonight | Site/night context, Night/Moon/Weather summaries, target selection/candidates, planner access and results due for recording. |
| Plan | Site/night, target and rig selection, capture blocks, opportunity/fit analysis, save, new plan and copy to another night. |
| Target candidates | Evaluates catalog targets against the selected night's conditions and preferences. |
| Night / Moon | Night timeline, darkness and altitude context, Moon information and calendar/night browsing. |
| Weather | Hourly forecast in compact rows or charts, details, local time, provenance, freshness and unavailable/partial data states. |
| Logbook | Saved sessions/results, filters, entry details, result recording, sharing/export and target progress. |
| Progress | Integration and session totals by target/filter from completed non-legacy sessions with recorded block counts. |
| Library | Manage rigs, targets and sites; detail/edit screens and scoped selection flows. |
| Metadata import | Android file selection, metadata review and equipment matching/confirmation before saving a rig. |
| Settings | Appearance, units, planning defaults, privacy, backup/data and About/licenses. |
| Database recovery | Reports unsupported database versions and offers an explicit reset flow. |

Bottom navigation contains Tonight, Logbook, Library and Settings.
Plan and detail/selection flows open separately above those tabs.

## Capture planning

- Ordered light, dark, flat, bias and dark-flat blocks with exposure/count,
  filter and contextual ISO/gain/binning settings.
- Calibration timing policies: in-window, outside-window or reused library.
  Helpers expose inherited settings and mismatch warnings.
- Budget includes integration, frame overheads and applicable optional
  setup, dither, refocus, filter-change and meridian-flip times.
- Camera class, tracking choice/override and applicable in-camera noise
  reduction affect the relevant planning calculations.
- Visibility/darkness/Moon and optional cloud gates determine usable windows.
  Fit compares plan load with opportunity and configured margins.
- Storage distinguishes file evidence, declared/measured sizes and theoretical
  estimates. Relative stacking gain does not claim absolute physical SNR.
- White balance, AF/MF and field provenance can be recorded.
  ISO/gain and AF/MF remain descriptive.
- Draft edits, saved snapshots and changed saved plans are distinct;
  leaving a changed plan offers Save/Discard/Cancel.

## Catalogs, sites and rigs

Targets support designation/common-name/alias search and custom entries.
Coordinates are J2000; unknown size and magnitude stay absent.
Rigs store camera/sensor/optics data, tracking, limits and provenance.
Sites store coordinates, optional elevation/time zone and manual Bortle/SQM.
GPS and a map can select a position; place-name lookup is optional.

Metadata readers cover DNG, JPEG, HEIF still images and FITS.
Recognition of a format does not imply a reader exists for it; unsupported
formats and unreadable files return explicit outcomes. Metadata is reviewed
before it creates or changes equipment.

## Results and data portability

Users report completed-as-planned, partial frame counts, or not done with an
optional reason; notes and observed conditions are optional.
Session snapshots retain saved context for history. Legacy logs remain readable.
There is no dedicated live-tracker screen.

Logbook supports text sharing, portable session-file export and AstroBin
acquisition CSV preview/sharing. AstroBin export is a file workflow.
Settings provides local backup and confirmed restore through a staged restart.

## Offline and presentation

Saved data, bundled catalogs and astronomy/planning calculations work offline.
Forecast retrieval, map tiles and optional place-name lookup use the network.
Weather retains source/fetch-time/cache information and missing-data states.
Night calculations use UTC; local display respects the site's time context.

Appearance supports System/Light/Dark plus a separate red field mode.
Display units and weather presentation are configurable.
The app plans and records; it does not acquire images or control hardware.

See [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for models/storage and
[Design system](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) for the implemented visual system.

  opportunities, budgets, fit, calibration, storage and session logic.
- `lib/domain/metadata/`: bounded file readers and metadata result types.
- `lib/domain/equipment_import/`: equipment matching and specification estimates.
- `lib/data/`: Drift persistence, SharedPreferences repositories, network/device
  adapters, metadata file access, export and backup implementations.
- `lib/core/`: math, clock, units, configuration, diagnostics and theme tokens.

UI calls ViewModels; ViewModels use domain interfaces and services.
Data adapters implement those interfaces. Astronomy/math calculations are
separate from Flutter presentation.

## State and navigation

`AppViewModels` constructs dependencies in `presentation/app_view_models.dart`.
Provider exposes shared ViewModel instances, predominantly through
`ChangeNotifierProvider`; lifecycle and candidate coordinators use `Provider`.
Widgets consume state through Provider reads and watches.

- `SiteViewModel`: active site, position and local-time context.
- `SessionPlanViewModel`: editable target, rig, night and capture blocks.
- `PlanLifecycleViewModel` / `CurrentSession`: restore, open, new, copy,
  save and discard of the current plan.
- `NightConditionsViewModel`, `CandidatesViewModel`,
  `CaptureAnalysisViewModel`: forecast/astronomy, candidates and plan analysis.
- `StartupViewModel` / `TonightViewModel`: loading and first-run/home state.
- `GearViewModel`, `TargetsViewModel`, `SessionsViewModel`: library/logbook state.
- `ResultsViewModel`, `MetadataImportViewModel`, `BackupViewModel` and
  `AstroBinExportViewModel`: their respective workflows.
- Settings, display, theme and disclosure ViewModels persist user choices.

`go_router` defines a stateful indexed shell for Tonight, Logbook, Library
and Settings. Plan, results, choosers and Night/Moon/Weather open above the tabs.
Router restoration returns to the appropriate list when object arguments
cannot be restored. The plan flow prompts for unsaved changes.

## Domain data

| Model | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `AstroTarget` / `TargetAlias` | Catalog/custom identity, J2000 RA/Dec in degrees, type, optional size/magnitude, source and searchable aliases. |
| `EquipmentProfile` | Flattened rig/camera view: sensor dimensions, resolution, pixel pitch, focal length/ratio, camera class, tracking, exposure limit and provenance. |
| `LocationProfile` | Coordinates, optional elevation, IANA zone, manual Bortle/SQM context, sources/dates and notes. |
| `CalendarDate` / `SessionNight` | Evening date and a half-open 24-hour UTC window beginning at site mean solar noon. |
| `CaptureBlock` | Frame type, exposure seconds, count, filter, binning, typed ISO/gain, calibration policy, white balance, AF/MF, origins and file evidence. |
| `SessionPlan` / `PlanOverrides` | Site/target/rig references, night, ordered blocks, labels, tracking override and optional per-plan budget/storage values. |
| `Session` / `SessionLog` | Lifecycle, references, timestamps, snapshots, blocks, counts, results and notes; legacy records remain readable. |
| `SessionSnapshot` | Versioned JSON of saved context, preferences, budget, opportunity and weather. |
| `ResultReport` | Completed as planned, partial per-block counts, or not done with optional reason and observed conditions. |
| `WeatherSnapshot` / `NightWeather` | Provider/model, fetch time, coordinates, hourly values, freshness, cache/failure/out-of-range state. |

`SessionStatus` includes `draft`, `planned`, `inProgress`, `completed` and
`abandoned`. Repository methods enforce lifecycle transitions. Execution
models, events and `ExecutionMachine` remain in the code; the router has no
dedicated live-tracker screen. Results are user reports of acquisition.

Night identity uses the site's evening date. Time contexts display an IANA
zone or mean solar time; DST changes local labels, not the UTC night window.
Unknown optional values are null. Units and provenance are explicit;
ISO/gain does not model photon collection.

## Persistence

`data/database/app_database.dart` defines Drift schema **27** in
`astroplan.sqlite` under the application documents directory.
The supported migration floor is version 8; unsupported older/newer databases
take the recovery path rather than being silently reinterpreted.

| Tables | Stored data |
| --- | --- |
| `Devices` → `CameraModules` → `OpticalRigs` | Device/camera/optics chain, specifications, provenance and capture-format evidence. |
| `LocationProfiles` | Saved sites and optional sky-quality context. |
| `AstroTargets`, `TargetAliases` | Targets and catalog-designation/name aliases. |
| `SessionLogs` | Session aggregate, status, references, timestamps, snapshots, overrides, result kind and notes. |
| `CaptureBlocks` | Ordered blocks, settings, calibration policy, evidence and completed/rejected counters. |
| `SessionEvents` | Ordered event history used to reconstruct execution state. |

SQLite foreign keys are enabled; blocks/events cascade with session deletion,
while camera/device references restrict deletion.
SharedPreferences stores planning/display/privacy/first-run preferences,
planner selection state and weather snapshots.
`FileBackupService` and `BackupStaging` validate and stage local restore;
startup applies it before opening the live database.

## External adapters and dependencies

- Open-Meteo weather through `http`, with cached snapshots.
- GPS through `geolocator`; device zone through `flutter_timezone`/`timezone`.
- OpenStreetMap tiles through `flutter_map`/`latlong2`; opt-in Nominatim lookup.
- Android file picker/range reads through a custom metadata platform channel.
- DNG, JPEG, HEIF still-image and FITS metadata readers in the domain.
- Backup uses `file_picker` and `archive`; export uses `share_plus`;
  external links use `url_launcher`.
- Drift code generation uses `drift_dev` and `build_runner`.

See [Product specification](PRODUCT_SPEC.md) and [Design system](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md).

external.name: figma
external.description: Use the Figma MCP server to fetch design context, screenshots, variables, and assets from Figma, and to translate Figma nodes into production code. Trigger when a task involves Figma URLs, node IDs, design-to-code implementation, or Figma MCP setup and troubleshooting.

external.name: figma-code-connect-components
external.description: Connects Figma design components to code components using Code Connect mapping tools. Use when user says "code connect", "connect this component to code", "map this component", "link component to code", "create code connect mapping", or wants to establish mappings between Figma designs and code implementations. For canvas writes via `use_figma`, use `figma-use`.

external.name: figma-create-design-system-rules
external.description: Generates custom design system rules for the user's codebase. Use when user says "create design system rules", "generate rules for my project", "set up design rules", "customize design system guidelines", or wants to establish project-specific conventions for Figma-to-code workflows. Requires Figma MCP server connection.

external.name: figma-create-new-file
external.description: Create a new blank Figma file. Use when the user wants to create a new Figma design or FigJam file, or when you need a new file before calling use_figma. Handles plan resolution via whoami if needed. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard)

external.name: figma-generate-design
external.description: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, screen, or view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles via search_design_system, imports them, and assembles screens incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

external.name: figma-generate-library
external.description: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

external.name: figma-implement-design
external.description: Translates Figma designs into production-ready application code with 1:1 visual fidelity. Use when implementing UI code from Figma files, when user mentions "implement design", "generate code", "implement component", provides Figma URLs, or asks to build components matching Figma specs. For Figma canvas writes via `use_figma`, use `figma-use`.

external.name: figma-use
external.description: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

external.name: imagegen
external.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

external.name: impeccable
external.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, simplify, harden, animate, or otherwise improve a frontend interface: websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, components, forms, settings, onboarding, empty states, and native iOS or Android screens. Handles UX review, hierarchy, layout, typography, color, motion, UX copy, accessibility, responsive behavior, edge cases, and capturing or documenting design systems (DESIGN.md, tokens). Also for making bland UI bolder, loud UI quieter, or ambitious visual effects. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

external.name: sites
external.description: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting.

external.name: sites-remix
external.description: Remix a Site built with the Sites plugin into a new Site. Use when the user has identified the source Site and asks to remix it.

external.name: audit
external.description: Audit or critique a product flow, journey, workflow, funnel, onboarding path, checkout path, settings path, screen, or multi-step product experience by capturing screenshots first, then reporting UX, design, and accessibility findings from that evidence. Default to an inline report; use a canvas for a visual walkthrough when requested or clearly implied by the ongoing task. Use when the user asks to audit, review, critique, inspect, assess, analyze, evaluate, or give feedback on a product experience.

external.name: design-qa
external.description: Internal prototype QA helper. Use only after a Product Design prototype, URL-to-code build, or image-to-code build has a source visual target and a rendered implementation to compare before handoff. Do not use for broad UX critique, design critique, product audits, or flow reviews; route those user-facing requests to audit.

external.name: get-context
external.description: Mandatory design-brief gate for clarifying the product and outcome. Use before ideation, image-to-code builds, redesigns, or product UI work to clarify missing product information and play back the brief before proceeding.

external.name: ideate
external.description: Generate image-based alternatives, remixes, or new design directions from a Product Design brief. Use when the user asks for design variants, visual exploration, remixes, or image-generated approaches from provided context.

external.name: image-to-code
external.description: Implement a selected image, screenshot, mockup, or Image Gen reference as a faithful, responsive frontend.

external.name: index
external.description: Use when Product Design is explicitly invoked, or when the user's main goal is to explore a design, research UX, audit or critique a flow, faithfully clone a visual source, check a built design, or share a prototype. Do not use Product Design for ordinary implementation unless the user explicitly asks for it.

external.name: research
external.description: Run fast, source-grounded UX research on the highest-signal problems users are experiencing with a user-specified digital product. Use when the user asks to research user pain, UX friction, onboarding issues, docs/help problems, developer experience friction, support pain, product workflow issues, or current user complaints for a named product.

external.name: share
external.description: Share a runnable prototype using the user's preferred deployment tool.

external.name: url-to-code
external.description: Clone a live URL as a runnable frontend-only local app.

external.name: user-context
external.description: Load or manage Product Design's saved user context. Use when the user asks to set up Product Design, get started, onboard, save product or design sources, see what Product Design remembers, update saved context, or remember Product Design preferences. Examples include product URLs, Figma files, screenshots, reference images, codebase paths, Storybook, tokens, design systems, brand assets, and general product/design notes.

external.name: impeccable
external.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

external.name: brand-identity
external.description: Collect a named organization's existing logo, color palette, fonts, and homepage messaging for a pitch deck, sales presentation, proposal, or other document. Use for requests such as making a slide match a company's website, finding the right logo and brand hex codes, or assembling a website-derived asset pack, even if the user never asks to scrape or search. Return sourced asset links and observed styling so the document can use the actual identity. Excludes inventing a brand, brand positioning advice, and styling from already sufficient supplied assets.

external.name: design
external.description: Extract an existing website's visual system into an implementation-ready DESIGN.md with design tokens, layout, components and image references. Use for recreating a site's visual style, building a page to match a reference URL, or documenting its UI patterns, even without an explicit request to scrape. Excludes creating a new brand and simple logo, color or font lookups for documents.

external.name: build-brand-palette
external.description: Build a distinctive, usable brand color system from an organization, product, audience, positioning, personality, industry, or existing brand color. Use for brand identity palettes, rebrands, campaign palettes, startup colors, or assigning brand color roles. Do not use for full UI themes, interior design, image extraction, or merely formatting existing colors as code.

external.name: compose-ui-theme
external.description: Compose a coherent application or website color theme from seed colors, an existing palette, a product brief, or light/dark-mode requirements. Use for UI surfaces, text hierarchy, controls, focus states, borders, and semantic feedback colors. Do not use for brand identity alone, interior spaces, or code-only token formatting without theme design.

external.name: direct-creative-palette
external.description: Translate an emotion, story, era, place, genre, sensory phrase, cultural reference, or abstract creative direction into an original editable palette. Use for evocative palettes, art direction, fictional worlds, campaigns, covers, events, and mood-led color exploration. Do not use for literal image extraction, formal brand systems, interior specifications, or UI role assignment.

external.name: extract-image-palette
external.description: Extract a purposeful editable color palette from an attached photo, logo, screenshot, artwork, mood board, or other visible reference. Use when users ask for colors from an image, a visual-reference palette, dominant or accent colors, or a palette inspired by an attachment. Do not trigger when no image is available or when the user wants the image edited rather than its colors analyzed.

external.name: generate-design-tokens
external.description: Convert a supplied or currently selected palette into semantic design tokens, color roles, and implementation-ready CSS variables, Tailwind theme values, or design-token JSON. Use for naming palette colors, creating primitive and semantic color layers, or preparing colors for a design system. Do not use to invent a broad brand identity, extract image colors, or design an entire UI without an input palette or seed.

external.name: harmonize-palette
external.description: Diagnose and repair an existing color palette that feels clashing, muddy, repetitive, unbalanced, too warm or cool, or otherwise incoherent while preserving its intent and specified anchor colors. Use for making supplied colors more cohesive or revising a current palette. Do not trigger for creating a palette from scratch unless the user provides a clear starting palette.

external.name: plan-interior-palette
external.description: Plan a practical interior color palette for a room or property using its function, orientation, natural and artificial light, dimensions, fixed finishes, furnishings, and desired atmosphere. Use for walls, trim, ceilings, cabinetry, upholstery, and decor color schemes. Do not use for exterior architecture, product UI themes, or brand palettes.

external.name: visualize
external.description: Create visualizations and interactive tools directly in conversation. Proactively use to show how something works; explore 'what happens when', 'what changes', or 'help me understand'; compare or inspect; create simulations, maps, charts, graphs, and mockups. Use standard tools for static scientific figures.

scope: All five project design skills and their supporting references, project governance pointers, current theme owners, plus design-facing skill copies discovered in the three listed local skill/cache roots. External copies are optional tools, not adopted Culmina rules; duplicate versions remain visible. Archived evidence is not active policy.
